title: Severe Pediatric Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infections Occurring in the Era of Antiviral Prophylaxis
official: Severe Pediatric Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infections Occurring in the Era of Antiviral Prophylaxis
summary:
Hospitalization for RSV lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) still occurs, including in infants having received nirsevimab/clesrovimab or born to mothers vaccinated with Abrysvo.

We hypothesize that pediatric patients hospitalized for RSV LRTIs occurring in the era of large use of prophylaxis, could be, at least in part, explained by virological factors (emergence/selection of variants with decreased susceptibility to prophylaxis) and/or immunological factors (inherited immune deficiency, presence of auto-antibodies neutralizing anti-viral cytokines such as type I interferons, impaired mucosal responses or mucosal pharmacokinetics issues inducing low levels of local concentrations of nirsevimab/clesrovimab).
conditions: Children <24 Months Hospitalized for RSV-related Lower Respiratory Tract Infection

interventions.name: Prior exposure to prophylactic treatment with Abrysvo or nirsevimab/clesrovimab

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Child \< 24 months
* Admission to the hospital for RSV-related lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI), on the basis of the treating physician's decision and a confirmation of RSV by means of a positive result of a test performed in accordance with routine clinical practice
* Informed consent of legal representative(s) of the child

Exclusion Criteria:

* Prior exposure to other RSV prophylaxis than maternal Abrysvo vaccine or nirsevimab/clesrovimab
* Admission not directly related to RSV-related LRTI, according to the investigator's judgment
* Nosocomial RSV-associated LRTI (defined by respiratory symptoms attributed to RSV occurring \>7 days after admission for another cause)
* No healthcare insurance
